structural.clause: §0C.28-ter, IntentRecord.c9_domain: "Mint class D, AUDIT_RETAINED. **Non-null IFF capability.space === 'C9'.** … On the run-bearing path an envelope whose capability.space is 'C9' and whose correlation.agent_id is null is REFUSED at EP-MINT; on the run-less capability-read path it is null by construction (§0C.28-quater)."
structural.conflictsWith: §0C.28-quater's normative block: "**On the run-less registered-capability-read path**, `c9_domain` is `null` **by construction**", read against §1.1.4 ("`run_id` is nullable because two paths mint envelopes: a coordination run and a registered capability read"), §4.1.1 L1 (minter 2 of 3 is "a registered capability read endpoint"), and §3.2's effect table (a `REFINE` carries a non-null `capability`, which §0B.7 fixes to the C9 space).
structural.consequence: The two sentences are in the SAME declaration and cannot both be satisfied. A run-less capability-read envelope — e.g. a SERVICE_SELECTOR minted from `catalog.services.read` whose `more_intent` is a REFINE carrying that same C9 key (§2.6.2) — has `correlation.agent_id === null` by construction, so `c9_domain` is null, while `capability.space === 'C9'`, so the IFF demands non-null. A validator enforcing the declared field invariant at EP-MINT refuses every such record. That is one of the three declared mint paths refusing every C9-bearing intent it composes — precisely the failure round 9 caught and repaired for the REFUSAL sentence while leaving the FIELD INVARIANT one line above it untouched. This is the §0C.17-quater defect class verbatim: the repair is inert because the signature it left standing disagrees with the call site it fixed.
structural.fix: Scope the invariant the way §0C.28-quater scopes the refusal: replace "Non-null IFF `capability.space === 'C9'`" with "Non-null IFF `capability.space === 'C9'` **and** `correlation.run_id !== null`; null on the run-less registered-capability-read path, where no run and therefore no registered agent exists." No other text changes; EC-11's second Gate 6 branch already reduces correctly on that path.

structural.clause: §0C.13 errata table, EC-6 ruling: "…and the name source is `nameSourceOf(ref, env)`, **total over `InteractiveRef`'s six members**…" and EC-17 ruling: "`InteractiveRef`'s **six** members are the typed authority". §0C.22-ter likewise: "`InteractiveRef` (§4.8) is a closed **six**-member union".
structural.conflictsWith: §0C.22-bis: "§4.8's InteractiveRef gains a **SEVENTH** member … `| { k: 'slot'; id: string }`"; `refKey` declared "total over the closed SEVEN-member union"; `nameSourceOf`'s switch carries seven cases ending "total by type over the closed seven-member union"; §0C.22-sexies: "`InteractiveRef` gains `{ k: 'slot'; id: string }` — a seventh member"; and EC-17's own paragraph at §0C.28-bis: "`InteractiveRef`'s members — **seven** after §0C.22-sexies adds `{k:'slot'}` — are the typed authority".

Under the six-member ruling the union has no member that can denote TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR's declared interactive path `groups[].slots[].slot_ref` (§2.6.4), so §2 K22's set-equality rule ("`reading_order` … must contain exactly the refs produced by `KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths`") is unsatisfiable for the booking flow's central kind and no TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR envelope is mintable — which is exactly the round-9 confirmed defect, reopened by the errata rows of the very erratum that closed it. `refKey` and `nameSourceOf`, both declared total, are simultaneously total over six and over seven.
structural.fix: Change "six members" to "seven members" in EC-6's ruling and in EC-17's ruling, and "a closed **six**-member union — `option`, `field`, `intent`, `row`, `entry`, `section`" to "a closed **seven**-member union — `option`, `field`, `intent`, `row`, `entry`, `section`, `slot`" in §0C.22-ter, and add `§0C.22-sexies` to EC-6's citation list (it currently cites only §0C.22, -bis, -ter, -quater, so the round-9 amendment is not referenced from the errata table at all).

security.clause: §0C.13 errata table, EC-4 ruling: "**Amended.** A **derived**, build-vetoed, non-actuating `FLOOR_EXEMPT` set — keyed on `priority === 0` plus three exclusion clauses, never on a list of names — **floors at `ANONYMOUS`**. Five intents satisfy it. SOURCE.3 gains `priority: 0`. Steps 2, 3, 5, 6 still apply. §0C.17"

The contract must not rest on 'no clause mints it at priority 0 today' — that is an accident of the current text, not a mechanism." The errata row restates the VOIDED first draft, so the hole §0C.17-ter closed is reopened by the same section's own errata table. It is not fail-closed unreachability: lowering a floor strictly widens reach. For `control.run.cancel` the owner endpoint's own principal/tenant lock ([EXISTS], `c9.store.ts:588–615`) is a surviving second fence; for `control.delivery.resolve` (P-17, `[ABSENT]`) no endpoint lock exists at all, so the zeroed `CONTROL_FLOOR` is the only declared fence on it.

structural.clause: §0C.22-quinquies: "§4.8.2 therefore gains a sixth column, **`accessible_name_suffix`**, populated for all twenty-two rows … The other sixteen carry the declared default `''` … so the rule is total over all twenty-two kinds with no \"otherwise\" branch left to interpretation" — with the STAFF_SELECTOR row's suffix `nearest_availability`, applied by A-2's mechanism "for every `ref ∈ a11y.reading_order` … and, for every kind §4.8.2 names, equality with the row's composition applied to the emitted body".
structural.conflictsWith: §2.6.3 StaffSelectorBody, which declares `any_staff_option: OptionItem | null` and names `any_staff_option.option_id` a declared interactive path, while `nearest_availability` is declared only on the `options[]` intersection type `OptionItem & { staff_ref; role_label; nearest_availability; rating }`. §2.3.3's `OptionItem` declares option_id, label, sublabel, badges, measures, media, intent_token, enabled — no `nearest_availability`.
structural.consequence: The suffix is keyed per KIND while A-2's obligation is quantified per REF, so a totality claim over kinds does not make the rule total over the refs it binds. Sharpest instance: `any_staff_option` is a declared interactive path denoted by a `{k:'option'}` ref, and the STAFF_SELECTOR suffix names a member its shape does not declare — the identical defect §0C.22-sexies filed for STRATEGY_OPTIONS.alternatives[] not being an OptionItem, one row over. The same hole recurs wherever a populated row's scope is narrower than the kind's declared paths and the kind is therefore not among "the other sixteen" that carry the empty default: SERVICE_SELECTOR's `more_intent` (the suffix is "each option's duration and price"; an intent ref has neither), STAFF_SELECTOR's `more_intent`, APPROVAL's `reject_intent` and `detail_intent` (the row scopes itself "on the approve control"), CLIENT_LIST's `table.rows[].row_key` refs (the row scopes itself "on `bulk_intents[]` only"), ARTIFACT's `regenerate_intent`. For those refs no composition is defined and none is derivable, so the CI check's second conjunct is either unsatisfiable or undefined, and the envelope cannot pass the accessible-name gate. A NORMATIVE-PENDING marking on P-19/P-31 does not excuse this: §0C.22-ter itself rules that "a NORMATIVE-PENDING rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have".

unproven.clause: §0C.28 (EC-10), PR2 (a′): "The emission validator refuses any intent whose `subjectCapability(i)` satisfies `RUN_OPENING` on an envelope whose `origin` is `PROACTIVE`. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`." — with `RUN_OPENING(ref) := ref.space === 'C9' ∧ (c9Registry.tryGet(ref.key)?.mode ?? 'PROPOSE_ONLY') !== 'READ'`.
unproven.whyUnproven: `RUN_OPENING` has no null branch, while §0B.30 declares `function subjectCapability(i: MintedIntent): CapabilityRef | null` and returns null for `NONE` and for every `NAVIGATE` whose target class is not 'c'. On a proactive envelope a null subject is not an edge case but the normal case, and in this contract version it is forced: S0.30 rules that class 'c' is "permitted on no kind in this contract version", so EVERY NAVIGATE now has a null subject; §4.9.1 PR1 permits NONE, NAVIGATE, REFINE and HANDOFF on a proactive envelope; §4.3 DR4 makes an appointment_reminder carry "intents of effect `NONE`, `NAVIGATE` or `HANDOFF` only"; §4.5.8's ANNOUNCEMENT row emits exactly one NAVIGATE; and S0.25's mandatory escape is `effect: 'NONE'`, `capability: null` on RICH_INTERACTIVE. So the predicate the rule quantifies over cannot be evaluated on the envelopes the rule governs: `ref.space` is read on null. The mechanism therefore does not do what the sentence says — it either raises at EP-MINT, in which case every proactive announcement envelope is unmintable and §4.9 dies fail-closed, or the implementer adds a guard the contract does not state. This is the defect §0C.28-quater repaired one erratum earlier for the c9_domain refusal ("the refusal as written would have made every C9 capability-read envelope unmintable"), and §0C.17-quater's `SENSITIVE_DEST` already sets the required pattern with its explicit `if (r === null) return false; // no destination named: nothing to classify`. EC-10 did not carry it. No errata row and no NORMATIVE-PENDING marking covers the gap: §0C.28's status binds P-24 for the CapabilityRef type, not for the predicate's domain.
unproven.fix: Restate the predicate ref-nullably and totally, exactly as SENSITIVE_DEST is stated: `RUN_OPENING(r: CapabilityRef | null) := r !== null ∧ r.space === 'C9' ∧ (c9Registry.tryGet(r.key)?.mode ?? 'PROPOSE_ONLY') !== 'READ'` — a null subject names no C9 capability, so it opens no run, and the fail-closed default on an unregistered key is unchanged. Add the totality statement to §0C.13's EC-10 row.

unproven.clause: §4.9.4 PR5b: "Each moment template declares `required_cells: string[]`. If any required Cell resolves to a non-`KNOWN` state at compose time, the emission is **suppressed** … *Mechanism:* the composer's suppression branch, driven by `required_cells` … *Evaluated at:* compose, before sealing." — together with §4.9.3 PR3b's "(i) `moment_template`: a frozen server template from **the closed moment-template registry** … *Mechanism:* the validator recomputes `narrative_hash` — against the template render for (i)".
unproven.whyUnproven: Both mechanisms name artefacts no shape in the contract declares. `required_cells` is a member of no declared interface: EC-14's `interface Moment { moment_key; notify_pref_key; once_per; quiet_hours_policy }` does not carry it, and no `MomentTemplate` type exists anywhere in the contract; the "closed moment-template registry" is named only here, and is distinct from both `MOMENT_REGISTRY` (keyed on moment_key, declared by EC-14) and `NARRATIVE_TEMPLATES` (§0.18/§1.6.5 P6, keyed by `narrative_template_id`, whereas ProactiveProvenance declares a separate `moment_template_id`). So a validator cannot render the template it must hash, and the composer cannot read the list it must suppress on. Neither clause is covered: §A2.8's blanket marking reaches only §4 mechanisms whose evaluation point resolves to EP-BUILD or EP-RENDER, and these resolve through §0.8 to EP-COMPOSE and EP-MINT; §0C.29 P-32's component list is "`MOMENT_REGISTRY`, `NOTIFICATION_CONSENT_REGISTRY` and `ProactiveProvenance.notify_pref_key`" and names neither; no §A1 row lists PR3b or PR5b under "Depends on it"; neither carries a *Status:* line of its own; and neither appears in §0.17, §0C.12, §0.16, §0B.9 or §0C.13. They are therefore unmarked normative claims whose mechanisms cannot be built as specified — the same defect EC-14 closed for PR3c's `notify_pref_key` and "the notification-consent registry", left standing two paragraphs over, and a direct breach of §0C.11-bis's own rule that "a normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares".
unproven.fix: Declare the missing carrier alongside EC-14's two registries and add it to P-32's component list: `interface MomentTemplate { moment_template_id: string; version: number; narrative_template_id: string; required_cells: string[] }` with `declare const MOMENT_TEMPLATE_REGISTRY: Readonly<Record<string, MomentTemplate>>`, and extend EC-14's EP-REGISTRY-LOAD assertion so that every MOMENT_REGISTRY row resolves a template, every template's `narrative_template_id` resolves in `NARRATIVE_TEMPLATES` (which keeps PR3b(i) inside §0.18's single prose-leaf rule) and every `required_cells` entry is a JSON Pointer the kind's leaf schema declares.

structural.clause: §0C.28-ter, `IntentRecord.c9_domain`: "Mint class D, AUDIT_RETAINED. **Non-null IFF `capability.space === 'C9'`.** Derived at EP-MINT from `Correlation.agent_id` …"

structural.consequence: For every capability-read envelope carrying a C9-space intent, the IFF requires `c9_domain` non-null and the path ruling requires it null. Both are normative, both sit inside Section 0-C, and no errata row reaches them — EC-11's row in §0C.13 mentions only that "`c9Capability`'s required `C9Domain` argument had no carrier, so `IntentRecord.c9_domain` is declared". No closed-shape clause can be written at EP-MINT from both. If the IFF governs, every run-less C9 envelope is refused at EP-MINT — precisely the defect §0C.28-quater exists to close (round 9's confirmed EC-11 finding), reopened one sentence above its own repair, and it takes METRIC, CHART, CLIENT_LIST, PROGRESS and ARTIFACT — the five kinds §0C.9 says EC-2 restored — back out with it.
structural.fix: Restate the shape clause as "Non-null IFF `capability.space === 'C9'` **and** `correlation.run_id !== null`; `null` on the run-less registered-capability-read path", so the IFF and §0C.28-quater state one rule instead of two.

structural.clause: §0C.22-quinquies: "§4.8.2 therefore gains a sixth column, **`accessible_name_suffix`**, populated for all twenty-two rows … The other sixteen carry the declared default `''` … so the rule is total over all twenty-two kinds with no \"otherwise\" branch left to interpretation", together with A-2 amended (§0C.22): "A control's accessible name is composed as `nameSourceOf(ref, env).label` + `', '` + *the `accessible_name_suffix` given by its kind's row in §4.8.2*", whose CI mechanism asserts "for every kind §4.8.2 names, equality with the row's composition applied to the emitted body".
structural.conflictsWith: The suffix is keyed on the KIND, but four of the six populated values name content only SOME of that kind's declared `reading_order` refs can supply. `STAFF_SELECTOR`'s suffix is `nearest_availability`, yet §2.6.3 declares `any_staff_option: OptionItem | null` — a bare `OptionItem` that declares NO `nearest_availability` (only the `options[]` elements are `OptionItem & { staff_ref; role_label; nearest_availability; rating }`) — and both `any_staff_option.option_id` and `more_intent` are declared interactive paths; a `more_intent` ref is `{k:'intent'}` and resolves to a `WidgetIntent` (§3.1), which declares none of these members. `SERVICE_SELECTOR`'s suffix is "each option's `duration` and `price`" while `more_intent` is in its paths. `APPROVAL`'s row scopes its suffix "on the approve control" while `reject_intent` and `detail_intent` are in its paths. `CLIENT_LIST`'s scopes it "on `bulk_intents[]` only" while `table.rows[].row_key` refs are in its paths.
structural.consequence: A-2's composition, declared total over all twenty-two kinds and asserted by equality per kind at `EP-BUILD`, is unsatisfiable for those refs, and §0C.22-bis makes `accessible_names` total over `reading_order` (`keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order.map(refKey))`, "an envelope whose `reading_order` names a ref with no entry is refused"). STAFF_SELECTOR is therefore unmintable whenever `any_staff_option` is non-null, and SERVICE_SELECTOR, APPROVAL and CLIENT_LIST are unmintable whenever they carry the `more`/`reject`/`detail`/row refs their own rows declare. This is round 9's confirmed `STRATEGY_OPTIONS.alternatives[]`-is-not-an-`OptionItem` defect one level up: the repair fixed which shape supplies the label and left the suffix keyed on the wrong granularity.
structural.fix: Type `accessible_name_suffix` as a per-ref-kind map — `Partial<Record<InteractiveRef['k'], string>>` with `''` as the declared default for every ref kind the row does not name — and write the four scoped rows as `{ option: 'duration, price' }`, `{ option: 'nearest_availability' }`, `{ intent: 'audience_size, risk_tier, reversibility' (approve control only) }`, `{ intent: 'audience_size' (bulk intents only) }`. Totality is then over kind × ref kind, which is the domain the rule actually ranges over.

structural.clause: §0C.28-bis EC-17: "per-kind membership is exactly what `KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths` produces — which is what K22's *mechanism* already says", and §2 K22: `reading_order` "must contain **exactly** the refs produced by `KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths` applied to this body … `validateEnvelope` recomputes the ref set from `interactive_paths` and refuses on any difference".
structural.conflictsWith: §0.25: "Every envelope whose `lifecycle.input_lock !== 'none'` … carries **exactly one** intent with `role: 'escape'`, `priority: 0`, never dropped by degradation"; §0B.36's `CONSENT_STATE` row: "focus lands on the heading; `change_handoff_intent` is a button in `reading_order`; **the escape is always keyboard-reachable**"; §4.8 A-5: "The escape intent is always keyboard-reachable"; A-3: "`a11y.reading_order` covers every interactive element and **DOM order equals it**"; and A-0's own mechanism: "the set of `InteractiveRef`s must equal the set of interactive elements derivable from the body **and the emitted intent list**, exactly". But `CONSENT_STATE`'s declared interactive paths (§2.6.18) are `change_handoff_intent` ONLY, and `TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR`'s (§2.6.4) are `groups[].slots[].slot_ref`, `more_intent`, `widen_window_intent`, `none_fit_intent` — while §0.29 counts the escape as its fifth intent ("select, more, widen, none-fit, escape").
structural.consequence: The escape is an emitted, undroppable, `priority: 0` intent (it is the first row of §0C.18's FLOOR_EXEMPT table), but on 18 of the 22 kinds — every kind except the four whose body declares a `dismiss_intent`/`discard_intent` path — no `interactive_path` produces a ref for it. K22 as reaffirmed by EC-17 therefore FORBIDS it from `reading_order`, so it has no `accessible_names` entry (which §0C.22-bis makes total over `reading_order`), is not in DOM order, and is not keyboard-reachable. §0B.36's `CONSENT_STATE` row and A-5 cannot hold, and A-0's derivation is falsified by the one control A-5 singles out. EC-17 sits in Section 0-C and outranks §4, so the conflict cannot be resolved by reading A-0's clause instead — it must be repaired.
structural.fix: Amend K22's derivation in EC-17 to `reading_order = refs(interactive_paths) ∪ refs(every emitted intent whose role is 'escape' or 'remedy')`, placing the escape last in render order; or give every `KindRule` an `escape_path` and populate it for the eighteen kinds that have no dismiss/discard handle.

structural.clause: §0C.13 errata, row EC-6: "the name source is `nameSourceOf(ref, env)`, total over `InteractiveRef`'s **six** members"; and row EC-17: "`InteractiveRef`'s **six** members are the typed authority".
structural.conflictsWith: §0C.22-bis: "§4.8's `InteractiveRef` gains a **SEVENTH** member … `| { k: 'slot'; id: string } // TimeSlotSelectorBody slot_ref`", with `refKey` declared "total over the closed **SEVEN**-member union"; §0C.22-ter's `nameSourceOf` closing comment "total by type over the closed **seven**-member union — no default branch is reachable"; and §0C.28-bis's own EC-17 body text "`InteractiveRef`'s members — **seven** after §0C.22-sexies adds `{k:'slot'}` — are the typed authority".
structural.consequence: The contract's masthead rule is "Where two sections of equal precedence conflict, **the later-numbered errata table governs** and says so explicitly" — so §0C.13 governs over §0C.22, and the union is six. Under six, `{k:'slot'}` is undeclared: TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR's declared interactive path `groups[].slots[].slot_ref` again has no member that can denote it, K22's set-equality rule is again unsatisfiable for the booking flow's central kind, `nameSourceOf`'s `case 'slot'` branch is dead code over an undeclared discriminant, and `refKey`'s totality claim is false. Round 9's confirmed structural defect is reinstated by the very errata table that records its repair — the precedence rule turns a stale count into the governing one.
structural.fix: Change both §0C.13 rows to "seven members" and have EC-6's row cite §0C.22-sexies alongside §0C.22-quater, as EC-17's body text already does.

structural.conflictsWith: §0.19 (S0.19), which deletes the member the second path traverses: "`PROGRESS.steps[].state: Cell<'PENDING'|'RUNNING'|'DONE'|'SKIPPED'>` with **`steps[].unknown` deleted** (its `reason_code`, `label` and `next_intent_ref` are the `Cell`'s own)." No errata row amends the path list — not §0.16 (E-1…E-31), not §0B.9 (EB-1…EB-15), not §0C.13 (EC-1…EC-17).
structural.consequence: `KIND_REGISTRY['PROGRESS'].interactive_paths` names a body member no shape in the contract declares. K22's validator "recomputes the ref set from `interactive_paths`" has nothing to walk, and `resolveInteractive` and `nameSourceOf` — both declared total over exactly the refs `interactive_paths` produces — have no element to resolve for that path. The consequence is not merely cosmetic: the remedy affordance that PROGRESS.1 ("a `next_intent_ref` that could resolve it"), PROGRESS.2 and §1.3 C5 make MANDATORY for any non-KNOWN step is thereby excluded from `reading_order`, gets no `accessible_names` entry, and is not keyboard-reachable — A-1 and A-3 fail on the one control an unknown step exists to offer.

structural.clause: §0C.26, Gate 8-R: "For a submission whose **`record.confirmation.requires_readback` is `true`**, the gateway refuses unless all four hold … A submission carrying `readback_ack` where `requires_readback === false` is **also** refused — the field is not an optional extra, and §0.54's closed-shape discipline is preserved in both directions."
structural.conflictsWith: §3.1 declares `confirmation: ConfirmationRequirement | null; // non-null iff effect ∈ {REQUEST_APPROVAL, COMMIT}`, and §3.7's `IntentRecord.confirmation` carries the same nullable type. §0C.26 places Gate 8-R "immediately after Gate 8 (input schema)" in §3.9's single ordered pipeline, which FR-5 requires to run with "no branch that skips a gate" — so Gate 8-R is evaluated on every submission, including the five effect classes whose record has `confirmation === null` (`NAVIGATE`, `REFINE`, `CONTROL`, `DRAFT`, `HANDOFF`).
structural.consequence: The gate's antecedent dereferences a member of a possibly-null object with no guard, so the gate is partial over the domain it is declared to run on. Read exactly as written, neither branch fires when `confirmation` is null — `requires_readback` is neither `true` nor `false`, it does not exist — so `readback_ack`, now a DECLARED optional member of `WidgetIntentSubmission` and therefore no longer caught by §0.54's unknown-key walk, is admitted on a `REFINE`/`DRAFT`/`HANDOFF` submission by neither branch. The concrete damage is that EC-11's repair is INERT on the one path that needs it: §0C.32 names it as a compensating fence for the nine floors EC-2 lowered — "What still fences these nine: their `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row, `CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR`, and — new in EC-11 — Gate 6's second C9 branch, `c9Capability`'s own admission" — and one of those nine, `a22.configuration`, is reachable by no affordance other than a handoff: §0C.9 calls it "the `a22.configuration` handoff", §0B.12 gap-blocks its COMMIT under `GAP-TENANT-CONFIG-COMMIT`, and §0B.39 keeps `TENANT_CONFIG_OWNER` gap-blocked on `SETTINGS_DRAFT`. It is an inert fence, which §0C.1 itself rules is not a fence: "A fence that holds because no current clause exercises the hole is not a fence."

unproven.whyUnproven: The mechanism cannot be invoked on the path that uses the key. EC-11's second C9 branch is guarded by `capability.space === 'C9'` and calls `c9Capability(record.capability.key, record.c9_domain, C9_REGISTRY_HASH)`. The two remaining named fences do not close the gap for this key by themselves: `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` is `[ABSENT]` (P-10, verified 0 occurrences repo-wide), and `CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR` is `ANONYMOUS` for `consent_class: 'none'`, which is what a tenant-configuration key would carry. Nothing is conferred — a handoff routes to a surface and invokes nothing — but the sentence claims a running check that, as specified, has no reachable call site for this key.
